blindSummary:
This state/province is the only one in the country that has not enacted any regional LGBTI or gender-identity law, a vacuum maintained across multiple legislatures. A regional equality bill proposed by the main opposition party (registered December 2024) only reached committee processing in June 2025 after the junior governing party abstained and the far-right party voted alone against; the far-right party is on record rejecting LGBTI subsidies here. The pending law is explicitly framed around stopping the documented exodus of LGBT people, especially young ones, from the region's rural areas to larger cities.

For a transgender visitor the practical effect of the legislative vacuum is the absence of a dedicated regional equality office, no institutional hate-crime observatory, and no region-specific administrative protocol for responding to gender-motivated incidents. National criminal law still applies and no criminal ban or facility restriction exists here, so the severity floor is set by the national framework. The region's comparatively large negative deviation from the country-wide baseline reflects the sub-national administrative coldness and rural exposure identified in the research as the country's real fault line, not any criminal threat specific to this region.

Compared with the capital region, which at least operated a trans law and an anti-LGBTI-phobia law before narrowing them, this state/province has never had the framework to narrow; the gap is legislative vacuum versus legislative rollback. Compared with two small overseas enclaves, this region's deviation is larger because its rural geography compounds the absence of any protective infrastructure and because the exodus pattern is regionally documented, whereas the enclaves' finding is statute-book only with no incident evidence.
